summary: POC scoping for Celeste Biotech: discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs. Agreed on a 4-week pilot focusing on integration + benchmarks. Success criteria will be defined around latency (p95), throughput (sustained qps), accuracy/regression tolerance on labeled set, and cost per 1M tokens. Initial plan: run hosted POC for speed, escalate to Dedicated if performance/cost tradeoffs warrant, and evaluate Private only if data residency or regulatory needs require it.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hi everyone, thanks for making time. quick intros?
[00:06] Lina: hi, lina ortiz, head of ml at celeste, we run diagnosis assistant workflows and some clinical notes summarization.
[00:13] Markus: markus voss, cto. i'm mostly here for infra/ops questions.
[00:17] Priya: priya shah, devops, will handle network/security.
[00:21] Daniel (Redwood SE): hey all, daniel park, i'll run through benchmarks and the scoping questions.
[00:26] Maya: goal today is to scope a 4 week poc — want to figure success criteria, traffic sizing, what to benchmark, and whether hosted, dedicated or private makes sense.
[00:35] Lina: yep, timeline is tight, we're targeting an internal demo mid april. key thing for us is p95 latency under 600ms for interactive use, and throughput around 30-50 qps for peak.
[00:47] Daniel: that's helpful. couple clarifying q's: what does a typical request look like? tokens per request, avg seq len?
[00:53] Lina: average prompt ~180 tokens, response ~240 tokens; some long cases up to 1k tokens but those are rare.
[01:01] Maya: ok so avg ~420 tokens roundtrip. for cost and perf estimates we'll assume 450-500 tokens per call.
[01:08] Markus: we also have compliance constraints — patient data is pseudonymized but we need audit logs and SOC2 evidence, plus we use internal KMS for keys.
[01:18] Priya: network wise we prefer VPC peering but if hosted api is used we need private link or egress controls.
[01:25] Daniel: makes sense. tradeoffs: hosted gives fastest time-to-value — simple REST / SDK and we can run benchmarks within a day. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity for predictable p95 and cost when volume is steady; Private/VPC gives full control for keys and residency but adds setup time.
[01:42] Maya: for the poc we often recommend starting hosted to validate quality and integration then switch to dedicated if the latency or cost bar is not met. private usually only if legal/regulatory forces it.
[01:52] Lina: what about accuracy/regression checks? we need to ensure model outputs don't drift; we'll have labeled cases.
[01:58] Daniel: we'll run a labeled 1k-sample evaluation and compute accuracy metrics and some custom criteria you define (precision on key fields). we'll also run n requests to measure p50/p95 and token throughput.
[02:09] Markus: what's the benchmark methodology?
[02:12] Daniel: suggested runbook: 1) smoke test integration, 2) single-client latency at different seq lengths (256, 512, 1024), 3) sustained qps ramp-up to target (10->50) for 10 minutes per step, 4) end-to-end labeled accuracy run on 1k samples. We'll capture p50/p95, gpu utilization, token/sec, cost estimates.
[02:29] Priya: how long does a hosted benchmark take?
[02:31] Daniel: end-to-end can be done in 48-72 hours if you provide data and we have connectivity. full runbook including optimizations 1-2 weeks.
[02:38] Lina: any caveats with caching or kv cache that would skew results?
[02:42] Daniel: yes — prefix caching and kv cache can reduce tokens and latency for repeated contexts. for fair results we'll disable application-level caching for the baseline run and then run a caching-enabled pass to show production gains. also we need to align on batching behavior because Redwood runtime uses adaptive batching.
[02:58] Markus: security — do you support SSO/SAML and audit logs?
[03:02] Maya: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs and integrates with customer KMS for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed keys or bring-your-own-kms for Private. we'll send SOC2 docs.
[03:13] Priya: if we do hosted, how do we handle VPC egress rules? we prefer PrivateLink.
[03:18] Maya: we can do AWS PrivateLink or set up VPC peering for Dedicated/Private. we'll include networking options in the doc.
[03:24] Lina: cost sensitivity — we have an internal target to keep inference costs under X per month, roughly ballpark. what are typical cost levers?
[03:31] Daniel: main levers are batching, quantized model variants, and caching. Dedicated often reduces per-token cost for steady workloads. hosted is easier initially but can be more variable at scale.
[03:40] Markus: curious about fallbacks — if the dedicated pool is saturated do you route to hosted as overflow?
[03:45] Maya: yes, smart routing and automatic fallbacks are available — you can set policies for latency-first or cost-first and have automatic model variant fallback.
[03:52] Lina: success criteria suggestion: p95 < 600ms on typical 450-token requests, sustained 40 qps with <70% GPU utilization, labeled accuracy delta <= 2% vs baseline, and cost estimate within 20% of our target.
[04:06] Daniel: that looks good. for the POC phases: week 1 integration (connect, auth, sample requests), week 2 baseline hosted benchmarks, week 3 optimization (batching/caching/quantization), week 4 review and decision — move to Dedicated or plan Private deployment if needed.
[04:21] Priya: how much setup for Dedicated?
[04:24] Maya: Dedicated provisioning typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and GPU type; we can do a burst-capacity bridge while Dedicated is provisioned.
[04:32] Markus: and Private on-prem?
[04:34] Daniel: Private/on-prem has more lead time (4-8 weeks) for packages and networking, also requires more ops effort on your side. we usually recommend Private only when data residency or corporate policy requires it.
[04:45] Lina: ok so plan is: start hosted POC to validate quality and integration, if latency/cost not acceptable then test Dedicated. If regulation requires, we evaluate Private in parallel but likely after initial validation.
[04:58] Maya: any blockers for the POC kickoff?
[05:00] Priya: need to confirm whether we can share pseudonymized dataset and if security can approve PrivateLink for traffic.
[05:06] Lina: i'll get the dataset ready and share access.
[05:09] Daniel: i'll prepare benchmark scripts and a runbook, we'll also include sample payloads tuned to your average 180/240 prompt/response pattern.
[05:17] Maya: i'll send pricing, SOC2, networking options and a proposed SOW.
[05:21] Markus: sounds good. timeline matches our internal demo.
[05:24] Maya: recap of next steps ... (brief recap)
[05:28] Lina: thanks everyone, looking forward to the kickoff.
[05:31] Maya: thanks, bye.
